newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bangemann says his angry reaction to question a mistake.
newsitem.headline: Bangemann says his angry reaction to question a mistake.

text.p: Industrial Affairs Commissioner Martin Bangemann said on Wednesday that at least part of his angry reaction to a question at a news conference last week had been a mistake.

Bangemann walked out of the news conference on industrial competitiveness after a German reporter asked whether Commission President Jacques Santer had urged him to be more active within the Commission.
He called the question "rubbish" and dismissed it as "a typical German problem".
On Wednesday during a news conference on the Internet, a representative of the International Press Association, criticised Bangemann for his behaviour.
"I think I made a mistake about generalising the matter," Bangemann replied. "I shouldn't have generalised about the German press as a whole."

He said he had reacted angrily because of the nature of the question. "It's always easy to criticise someone with an argument that's a bit far-fetched," he said. "Then the answer from the person who is attacked is a 'dementi' (denial)."
The press in a democracy should be vigilant without using "slightly unfair methods which gives a wrong image to both a politician or the press itself," he said.
